Reed-Solomon encode, recover, FFT, PPT, and linearity tests.

# Purpose
This file is a test and benchmark program for the `fd_reedsol` Reed-Solomon implementation. It includes unit tests for error strings, encode and recover state machines, parity generation, erasure recovery, and corruption detection. It also checks algebraic properties of the field operations and the transform functions used by the Reed-Solomon code, including FFT, IFFT, and PPT variants. The [`main`](<#main>) function initializes the runtime, creates a random number generator, runs all tests, runs performance measurements, and then shuts down.

A large part of the file is a reference encoder, [`fd_reedsol_encode_ref`](<#fd_reedsol_encode_ref>), which builds parity shreds by using matrix inversion and finite-field arithmetic over GF(2^8). The file compares the library output against this reference for many shred counts and shred sizes. It also defines helper wrappers around generated FFT, IFFT, and PPT functions so the tests can verify linearity, inverse behavior, and basis-vector results. In addition, it measures encode and recover throughput for several input patterns and prints the results.
